clue.text: Orpheus finally going to underworld for hints

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the name, so only its closing letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the mythical musician's name
Hades is the Greek underworld

explanation.surface: Orpheus descending to the underworld to rescue Eurydice, picking up clues on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Orpheus fits the underworld picture so well that it seems part of the scene, but only its tail letter counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades of meaning are slight differences or nuances, so the plural word can stand for subtle hints or suggestions.

clue.text: Trials new English and Scottish flag

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the preceding word's letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Fresh trials of English and Scottish flags, as if testing new national banners.
explanation.definitionFit: The saltire, a white diagonal cross on blue, is the St Andrew's cross flown as the national flag of Scotland.

clue.text: A fellow spy?

parts.note: taken as written
a gent, short for gentleman, is a fellow or chap

explanation.surface: A question asking whether some man is himself a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the whole clue also reads as a definition: a spy is a fellow operative.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is someone working secretly for an intelligence service, which is exactly what a spy does.

clue.text: No longer around, former partner can go to court

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a tin is a can
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A divorce story: the former spouse, no longer in the picture, is free to take the matter to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like the verb 'is able to', but it is the noun meaning a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A species that has died out completely is extinct, meaning it no longer exists anywhere around us.

clue.text: Hit barrier at work

parts.note: a wall is a barrier
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone at work punching or bumping into a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallop is a heavy blow, and to wallop someone is to strike them hard, so it serves as a verb for hit.

clue.text: Disinclined to be part of lifesaver's experiment

indicators.note: something that is part of the following words sits inside them, running across their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to take part in a lifeguard's trial run.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means having a strong dislike of it and therefore being unwilling or reluctant.

clue.text: Service man licensed by bishop to brew dreary ale

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so the letters that follow are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A churchman given the bishop's licence to make some dull beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service man' suggests the armed forces, but here the service is a church one.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Church of England a lay reader is an unordained person licensed by the bishop to lead some church services.

clue.text: Essential part of diet is not ripe, unfortunately

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is one where things have gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a key food in someone's diet has not yet ripened.
explanation.definitionFit: Protein is one of the main nutrients the body needs for growth and repair, so it is a necessary component of eating.

clue.text: Had scene rewritten to include analyst getting malicious pleasure

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes into the middle of the other
rewritten text has been redone, so the opening words' letters are set down in another order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged
Sigmund Freud, the founder of psychoanalysis

explanation.surface: A dramatist reworks a scene to bring in a psychiatrist who enjoys others' misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters are split so the analyst sits just before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: This German loanword names the pleasure someone takes in another person's misfortune, a spiteful kind of enjoyment.

clue.text: Reportedly uninteresting fruit

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: a slow film or book is dull and uninteresting

explanation.surface: Word has it that some fruit is rather boring.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloe is the small, sour, blue-black berry of the blackthorn, used to flavour sloe gin.

clue.text: Fine pass for unruly boy at centre of row

parts.note: a ticket is a pass allowing entry

indicators.note: an unruly child will not behave or stay in line, so the letters of the word it describes are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the letter in the very middle is used

parts.note: the middle of the three letters

explanation.surface: A ticket handed to a badly behaved boy in the middle of a row of seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a penalty to go with 'pass' and 'unruly', but it means all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickety-boo is old-fashioned British slang meaning everything is in order, all right or going smoothly.

clue.text: Pay attention to silent movement

indicators.note: movement means shifting position, so the letters of the word before it are moved around

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to concentrate on a quiet passage of a symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' suggests a section of a piece of music, but it is the signal to shift letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen to something is to give it your attention by hearing it carefully, so it matches the transitive phrase.

clue.text: Responded to article by son and wife before daughter

parts.note: an indefinite article
S is the abbreviation for son
W is the abbreviation for wife
ere is a poetic word for before
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A family reply to a newspaper piece, with son and wife getting in ahead of daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' reads as a newspaper item, but it is the grammatical word.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer something, such as a letter or question, is to respond or reply to it, so the past tense fits.

clue.text: About to get Grauniad's ultimate compiler a dog

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the closing letter of the paper's nickname is taken

parts.note: Grauniad is the jokey nickname for the Guardian newspaper, famed for typos; this is its last letter
a setter is the compiler of a crossword

explanation.surface: A Guardian crossword compiler is about to acquire a pet dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian, which published this puzzle, is nicknamed the Grauniad for its misprints.
explanation.definitionFit: The red setter, or Irish setter, is a breed of gundog with a glossy chestnut coat.

clue.text: Plan to find valuable stone under layers of rock

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word placed under another is written below it, so the stone is sent second after the layers

parts.note: strata are layers of rock
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A geologist's scheme to dig a precious stone out from beneath rock beds.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' places the stone below, that is after, the layers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme or trick devised to outwit someone, so it is a kind of plan.

clue.text: Good intentions involving god

indicators.note: involving means containing, so the answer lies within the words before it

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A worthy plan that brings a deity into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology, the all-father who rules over Asgard.

clue.text: Revolutionary listened to records

indicators.note: what is listened to is heard rather than read, so the sound of the next word matters, not its spelling

parts.note: marks are records, as of scores or grades

explanation.surface: A radical sat listening to his LP collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Marx, author of The Communist Manifesto, is the archetypal revolutionary thinker of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Member raising support given gin cocktail at get-together

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts a word upwards, so it reads from bottom to top
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters beside it are mixed up

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An MP raising a toast with a gin cocktail at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin cocktail' looks like a drink, but 'cocktail' just mixes the three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting is an occasion when people come together, which is what a get-together is, if more formally.

clue.text: Bad time of year to make babies?

parts.note: food that has gone off is bad
spring is a season

explanation.surface: Asking whether some season is the wrong one for conceiving children.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring is traditionally the breeding season, which makes the 'bad' reading playfully perverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are the children or young of a parent, so the word covers babies in the collective sense.

clue.text: Special gold poured into Scotsman's pouch

parts.note: SP is an abbreviation for special
or is the heraldic word for gold
a liquid that poured ran

explanation.surface: Pouring precious gold into a Highlander's purse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poured into' looks like a container instruction, but 'poured' supplies letters and 'into' merely joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is the leather or fur pouch hung at the front of a Scottish kilt, since kilts have no pockets.

clue.text: Gets smaller new missiles

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
arrows are missiles fired from a bow

explanation.surface: A shrinking stock of newly made weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' would usually signal a shuffle; here it is simply the letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that narrows becomes less wide, so as a verb it means decreases in size or gets smaller.

clue.text: One doing weaving with dye

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: weaving interlaces threads, so the letters of the word before it are interlaced into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A weaver at work with a colouring agent for cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue colouring obtained from plants and used for centuries to colour fabric such as denim.

clue.text: Senator's sounding strained after judgment

parts.note: Sen is the abbreviation for senator

indicators.note: sounding means as heard out loud, so the following word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: someone strained is tense

explanation.surface: A politician sounds stressed after a court ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is', joining the abbreviation to the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is the punishment a judge pronounces in court, so it is a legal judgment on the convicted.

clue.text: Cantankerous individual welcoming king to railway

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: one is a single individual
R is short for rex, Latin for king
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A grumpy man shows the king round to the railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornery is a chiefly American dialect word, from ordinary, for someone bad-tempered and difficult to deal with.

clue.text: Northern race excited by mother-of-pearl

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern

indicators.note: excited things are agitated and stirred up, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A people from the north thrilled at the sight of a shimmering shell lining.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is the iridescent material lining oyster and mussel shells, also known as mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Chuck out note found in campanologist's file

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so the first pieces sit within the last

parts.note: a campanologist is a bell-ringer
to bin something is to throw it away
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer's folder has been thrown away, along with a note inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring binder is a stiff folder with metal rings that hold punched sheets, a common kind of office file.

clue.text: Shoe made from carpenter's first piece of wood

indicators.note: first points to the opening of the word, so only its initial letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: A carpenter's maiden effort: footwear carved from a block of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A clog is a heavy shoe with a thick wooden sole, traditional in the Netherlands and northern England.

clue.text: Lark about with doctor in prison

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the medic's letters go within the jail

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Fooling around with the doctor while behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: To gambol is to skip and leap about playfully, like a lamb, which is what larking about means.

clue.text: 16's collaborator points to broken legs

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north

indicators.note: something broken has fallen apart, so the letters of the word after it are reassembled differently

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone points at a pair of broken legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 refers to the answer at 16 across, the revolutionary thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels co-wrote The Communist Manifesto with Karl Marx and edited Das Kapital after his death.
